concepts.name: Pointer hit-testing retains the initial dispatch chain
Single measurement per child in a layout pass
Consumption marks pointer changes without stopping propagation

questions.prompt: In Compose, a finger presses inside a custom draggable and then moves outside its bounds without lifting. What happens to subsequent events for that pointer?

choices.text: Every composable under the new position joins the original chain
All pointer events stop when the finger leaves those bounds
They continue through the original hit-tested chain
Each move performs a new hit-test and replaces that chain

questions.explanation: For non-hover pointer events, Compose hit-tests the pointer initially and retains that chain. Moving outside bounds does not automatically stop delivery or enroll new nodes. Hover has different rules.

sources.title: Understand gestures
sources.claim: A pointer is hit-tested initially and later non-hover events follow that chain even outside bounds; consuming an event does not stop propagation, so custom handlers must check isConsumed.

questions.prompt: A custom Compose `Layout` measures the same child with small constraints, then measures it again with larger constraints during the same measurement pass. What is wrong?

choices.text: Compose forbids measuring that child twice in one pass
Compose permits it when both measurements run on the main thread
Compose requires three measurements before placing each child
Compose permits it if the child uses a stable data model

questions.explanation: Compose does not support multi-pass measurement of the same child in a layout pass. Main-thread execution or stability does not waive the rule; measure children, choose size, then place them.

sources.title: Custom layouts
sources.claim: Compose does not allow measuring the same child multiple times in one layout measurement pass; measure children, choose parent size, then place the measured children.

questions.prompt: A custom Compose child handler calls `PointerInputChange.consume()`, but its parent custom handler still reacts. Which statements explain the behavior? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Consumed changes are invisible to every later pointer handler
Consumption marks the change instead of stopping propagation
Consumption removes the parent from the pointer dispatch chain
The parent should check `isConsumed` before acting on the change
Custom gesture code must handle consumption explicitly

questions.explanation: consume marks the change and downstream handlers can observe isConsumed. Custom handlers must check it and choose not to act. Consumption neither removes nodes from the chain nor hides the event from subsequent handlers.

sources.title: Understand gestures
sources.claim: A pointer is hit-tested initially and later non-hover events follow that chain even outside bounds; consuming an event does not stop propagation, so custom handlers must check isConsumed.

questions.prompt: Two overlapping Compose buttons are siblings at the same level. With default pointer dispatch, which button is hit when a finger presses inside both?

choices.text: Both siblings, regardless of their z-index values
The eligible sibling with the largest measured area
The eligible sibling with the highest z-index
The eligible sibling declared first in source order

questions.explanation: Default hit-testing chooses the highest-z eligible sibling. It does not broadcast to all overlapping siblings or choose by declaration order or area; custom pointer nodes can change sibling-sharing behavior.

sources.title: Understand gestures
sources.claim: A pointer is hit-tested initially and later non-hover events follow that chain even outside bounds; consuming an event does not stop propagation, so custom handlers must check isConsumed.

questions.prompt: After measuring children in a custom Compose layout, what is the normal next sequence?

choices.text: Place unmeasured children, then determine all their sizes
Draw every child before deciding the parent layout dimensions
Measure every child repeatedly until its preferred size stabilizes
Determine the parent size, then place the measured children

questions.explanation: The documented sequence is measure children, decide the layout size, then place children. Placement follows measurement; repeated measurement and drawing first are not that layout protocol.

sources.title: Custom layouts
sources.claim: Compose does not allow measuring the same child multiple times in one layout measurement pass; measure children, choose parent size, then place the measured children.

questions.prompt: Custom Compose gesture handlers listen to pointer-event passes. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Consuming a change automatically removes parents from every later pass
Final clears all consumption flags before parent handlers can see them
Custom handlers should check consumption before reacting
Initial travels from the root toward the leaves
Main travels from leaves toward the root, giving children precedence

questions.explanation: Main travels upward and Initial downward. Consumption remains observable through propagation; custom handlers must respect it. Final does not clear the flag, and consume does not remove parents.
